title: Assembling integer shift coherence along an object-covering family
statement: Let B and C be categories with integer shifts, V : B ⥤ C, and J_i : A_i ⥤ B a family of shift-commuting functors literally covering every object of B. Suppose each J_i ⋙ V has an integer CommShift structure c_i. If natural shift isomorphisms e_n for V precompose, using the J_i shift comparison, to the isomorphisms of c_i, then e_n satisfy the zero and addition axioms and define a CommShift structure on V. The construction uses the specified e_n as its shift isomorphisms.

source.place: Formal categorical assembly of shift coherence after checking finite representatives

proof.text: Precomposition with J carries the zero comparison to the composite zero comparison, and carries isoAdd(e_a,e_b) to the sum of the two precomposed comparisons. Prove these identities componentwise, using naturality of e_b and the zero/addition laws for J. At an arbitrary object P choose a literal representation J_i K = P. Cancel the isomorphism V.map(J_i.commShiftIso) and apply the zero or addition law of c_i. This proves both global laws.

proof_origin.place: K6: proved categorical cancellation for the finite-inclusion object cover

def assembleShift
    {I : Type*} {A : I → Type*} [∀ i, Category (A i)]
    {B C : Type*} [Category B] [Category C]
    [∀ i, HasShift (A i) ℤ] [HasShift B ℤ] [HasShift C ℤ]
    (J : ∀ i, A i ⥤ B) [∀ i, (J i).CommShift ℤ]
    (hJ : ∀ P : B, ∃ i K, (J i).obj K = P) (V : B ⥤ C)
    (c : ∀ i, (J i ⋙ V).CommShift ℤ)
    (e : ∀ n : ℤ, shiftFunctor B n ⋙ V ≅ V ⋙ shiftFunctor C n)
    (he : ∀ i n, precompShift (J i) V n (e n) = (c i).commShiftIso n) :
    V.CommShift ℤ
